evidence: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/lib/errorHandler.ts:221 — parseErrorResponse returns `message: data.message || errorInfo.message`, PREFERRING the raw server-supplied `data.message` string over the localized `errorInfo.message` (which errorCopy() resolves from the i18n bundle via i18n.t(`errors.catalogue.${code}.message`)). For the common case — any structured backend error whose body carries a `message` field — the client-side i18n catalogue is bypassed and the server's (untranslated, backend-default English) message is rendered to the user regardless of the active sk/cs/de locale.

Same pattern in the generic Error fallback at errorHandler.ts:190-196: the `if (error instanceof Error)` branch returns `message: error.message || copy.message`, surfacing a raw JS Error message (e.g. a technical TypeError string, or a library's English `message`) to the user-facing toast instead of the localized default copy.

This is the INCOMPLETE-FIX residue of the already-done finding code-review-ppt-web-core-errorhandler-i18n-gap (filed 2026-08-17, merged): that fix correctly i18n'd the catalogue itself (ERROR_MESSAGES/DEFAULT_ERROR -> errorCopy()/i18n.t, and the 429 branch), but it never touched these two `|| fallback` sites, so the localized copy it added is skipped whenever a server/JS message is present. Net-new vs backlog: the filed finding's evidence enumerated parseApiError/parseErrorResponse/parseHttpStatusError/429-branch as hardcoded-English but did NOT call out the message-preference ordering; no other ppt-web-core signal covers it.

Impact: LOW (locale-correctness / UX on user-facing error toasts; no functional break — data.message is still informative, just not localized). Nuance worth preserving in the fix: `data.message` sometimes carries dynamic specificity the generic catalogue copy lacks (e.g. 'Email already registered'), so the correct fix is NOT to blindly drop it — prefer the i18n catalogue copy whenever `data.error` resolves to a KNOWN catalogue code (errorCopy already distinguishes known vs unknown), falling back to `data.message` only for unknown codes; and for the `instanceof Error` branch, keep `error.message` only for dev/unknown and otherwise use the localized default.
